question: Why does using the identity function as an activation make a deep network effectively linear?
direct_answer: Because composing linear layers with no nonlinearity collapses to one linear map.
expanded_answer: If every layer is linear, then stacking layers does not create new kinds of transformations; the whole network can be rewritten as a single affine transformation. Nonlinear activations are what prevent this collapse and allow richer function classes.
key_points: Linear maps compose to linear maps
common_wrong_ideas: More layers always mean more expressiveness
A bias term alone makes the network nonlinear
Identity is a useful hidden-layer activation
